archetypes.note: Standard Wild Rift build. Focuses on Luden's Echo, Infinity Orb, and Rabadon's to maximize one-shot potential on squishies.
Leverages Awakened Soulstealer for ultimate resets and magic pen, synergizing perfectly with her innate takedown resets.
Splashing Crown of the Shattered Queen or Banshee's Veil is common to survive heavy dive or burst.
Liandry's Torment or Riftmaker. Suboptimal because Ahri excels at quick burst and repositioning, not extended DPS.
Ahri has zero AD scalings. Building attack damage or crit is entirely a trap.
Completely wastes her mobility and damage-focused kit.

flexPatterns: One defensive AP item like Crown of the Shattered Queen late.
Awakened Soulstealer early for ultimate resets and snowballing.
Morellonomicon flexed in against heavy enemy healing.
Ahri.identitySummary: Highly mobile AP burst mage and assassin. Relies on magic penetration, high AP, and ability haste to secure picks and snowball teamfights.

archetypes.note: The standard scaling path. E scales with crit damage and attack speed, making Infinity Edge and Magnetic Blaster core.
Blade of the Ruined King and Wit's End are massive early spikes because his E rapidly applies on-hit effects.
Tempting for Q/R burst, but vastly inferior to Crit/On-hit for his primary damage tool (E).
A single defensive AD item like Guardian Angel or Maw of Malmortius is acceptable late game.
Akshan has no AP ratios that justify building magic damage items.
Akshan requires pure offensive stats to function as an assassin/marksman.

flexPatterns: Blade of the Ruined King is the standard first item spike before building crit.
Wit's End is frequently rushed against heavy AP mid laners.
Exactly one defensive item (Guardian Angel) late game to ensure revives.
Akshan.identitySummary: A roaming marksman-assassin who relies on on-hit effects and critical strikes to maximize his swing (E) and double-shot burst.

counterplay: Hard CC to interrupt his swing
Burst damage to kill him quickly

archetypes.note: Standard path. Focuses on HP, resistances, and utility to survive engages and peel for carries.
AP ratios exist, but building AP sacrifices his core identity as an unkillable frontline. A trap in ranked.
His passive heal is too unreliable and small to justify healing or shielding power items.
No AD scaling, slow attack speed, and zero auto-attack synergy.

flexPatterns: Rushing Dead Man's Plate early for map-wide roam speed.
Adapting boots enchant to Protobelt for engage or Gargoyle for survival.
Building Thornmail if enemies have high sustain and healing.
Alistar.identitySummary: Alistar is a premier engage tank support who builds pure defensive and utility items to survive diving into the enemy team.

counterplay: True damage to bypass ultimate mitigation

archetypes.note: Standard WR path. BotRK into Trinity Force or Divine Sunderer, followed by survivability like Sterak's Gage or Death's Dance.
Blade of the Ruined King is mandatory. Wit's End is a common flex against magic damage.
High risk, high reward. Shieldbow or Mortal Reminder are good, but full crit is often too squishy for WR teamfights.
Snowball reliant. Lacks the durability needed to secure the crucial first reset in even games.
Viego needs offensive stats to kill targets and trigger his passive resets.
W has an AP ratio, but building AP is a complete trap.

flexPatterns: Swap Trinity Force for Divine Sunderer against tank-heavy comps.
One or two heavy defensive items like Amaranth Twinguard late game.
Wit's End as a magic resist option synergizing with on-hit.
Viego.identitySummary: A reset-reliant skirmisher who builds on-hit and bruiser items to survive long enough to secure his first possession and snowball teamfights.

counterplay: Anti-heal to reduce his innate sustain
Hard CC to burst him before he resets
Armor to mitigate his physical damage
Guardian Angel to deny his resets
